summary.title: Dense-TSNet: Dense Connected Two-Stage Structure for Ultra-Lightweight Speech Enhancement
summary.authors: Zizhen Lin, Yuanle Li, Junyu Wang, Ruili Li
summary.executive_summary: This paper proposes Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network designed for resource-constrained environments. The primary motivation is the high complexity of existing deep neural network models, which limits their deployment on edge devices like smartphones. The authors address the performance bottlenecks of narrow lightweight models, specifically the issue of uneven loss landscapes that cause early convergence. To solve this, they introduce a novel Dense Two-Stage (Dense-TS) architecture. Unlike the classic Two-Stage (TS) architecture, which uses a dilated dense block, Dense-TS replaces these with densely connected Two-Stage modules. This design ensures a smoother loss landscape, allowing for more robust refinement of the objective function in later training stages. Additionally, the paper introduces the Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB), a feature extraction module based entirely on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to ensure practical adaptability and efficiency. The MVGB captures features from three perspectives: global (via Large Kernel Extractor), channel (via Channel Attention), and local (via Learnable-Sigmoid Gate). The study also investigates the impact of loss functions on perceptual quality. While Metric Loss can improve objective scores like PESQ, it may negatively impact subjective perception by introducing distortions. Therefore, the authors propose using a Consistency Magnitude Loss to reconstruct speech signals. Experimental results on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset demonstrate that Dense-TSNet achieves a PESQ score of 3.05 with only 14K parameters. This represents a significant advancement, as it is the first model to achieve competitive speech enhancement performance at the approximately 10k parameter scale. The model outperforms the classic TS structure with similar parameter counts, validating the effectiveness of the dense connections in narrow architectures. The work contributes to the field by providing a viable, high-performance solution for real-world, low-resource speech enhancement applications.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper proposes Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network designed for resource-constrained environments. The primary motivation is the high complexity of existing deep neural network models, which limits their deployment on edge devices like smartphones. The authors address the performance bottlenecks of narrow lightweight models, specifically the issue of uneven loss landscapes that cause early convergence. To solve this, they introduce a novel Dense Two-Stage (Dense-TS) architecture. Unlike the classic Two-Stage (TS) architecture, which uses a dilated dense block, Dense-TS replaces these with densely connected Two-Stage modules. This design ensures a smoother loss landscape, allowing for more robust refinement of the objective function in later training stages. Additionally, the paper introduces the Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB), a feature extraction module based entirely on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to ensure practical adaptability and efficiency. The MVGB captures features from three perspectives: global (via Large Kernel Extractor), channel (via Channel Attention), and local (via Learnable-Sigmoid Gate). The study also investigates the impact of loss functions on perceptual quality. While Metric Loss can improve objective scores like PESQ, it may negatively impact subjective perception by introducing distortions. Therefore, the authors propose using a Consistency Magnitude Loss to reconstruct speech signals. Experimental results on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset demonstrate that Dense-TSNet achieves a PESQ score of 3.05 with only 14K parameters. This represents a significant advancement, as it is the first model to achieve competitive speech enhancement performance at the approximately 10k parameter scale. The model outperforms the classic TS structure with similar parameter counts, validating the effectiveness of the dense connections in narrow architectures. The work contributes to the field by providing a viable, high-performance solution for real-world, low-resource speech enhancement applications.

Research Context
Speech enhancement technologies are vital for improving clarity in noisy environments. Recent advancements have focused on deep neural networks, particularly the Two-Stage architecture. However, the complexity and size of these models limit their applicability in resource-constrained scenarios. Narrow lightweight models often encounter performance bottlenecks due to uneven loss landscapes. Advanced operators like Transformers or Mamba may lack practical adaptability compared to CNNs. Research on single-channel speech enhancement models with around 10k parameters is still limited.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question is how to design an ultra-lightweight model that overcomes early convergence limitations. The hypothesis is that a Dense Two-Stage structure ensures more robust refinement of the objective function. It is predicted that dense connections will provide a smoother loss landscape for narrow models. The authors hypothesize that Multi-View Gaze Block enhances feature extraction via global, channel, and local views. It is hypothesized that relying solely on Metric Loss may negatively impact subjective perception. The goal is to achieve competitive performance with a compact model size of around 14K parameters.

Methodological Details
The study utilized the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset for experiments. Speech samples were segmented into two-second intervals for the short-time Fourier transform. The STFT employed an FFT size of 400, a window length of 400, and a hop length of 100. The training process was conducted with a batch size of 2. The AdamW optimizer was used for the training process. Training was carried out for up to 1,000,000 steps. Evaluation metrics included PESQ, CSIG, CBAK, and COVL. The model size is approximately 14K parameters. The model has 356M MACs.

Procedures And Architectures
The speech signal is processed using Short-Time Fourier Transform to convert it to the time-frequency domain. Dense-TSNet inputs only the magnitude spectrum and performs time-frequency feature extraction. The Dense-TS structure replaces dilated convolutions in the Dilated Dense Block with Two-Stage modules. Features are mapped to a high-dimensional space using 1x1 convolutions. The encoder omits the dilated dense block and proceeds directly to the Two-Stage feature extraction block. The Multi-View Gaze Block consists of Large Kernel Extractor, Learnable-Sigmoid Gate, and Channel Attention. The Large Kernel Extractor uses large kernel depthwise convolutions to capture long-range low-frequency features. Channel Attention reallocates weights to each channel to focus on important channels. The Learnable-Sigmoid Gate establishes local spatial perspectives using depth-wise and point-wise convolutions. The Consistency Magnitude Loss computes the minimum distance between twice-STFTed speech and clean speech. The Metric Loss integrates objective evaluation metrics via a discriminator.

Key Results
Dense-TSNet achieved a PESQ score of 3.05 on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset. The model achieved a CSIG score of 4.51. The model achieved a CBAK score of 3.58. The model achieved a COVL score of 3.86. The model size is 14K parameters. The model has 356M MACs. The classic Two-Stage structure achieved a PESQ score of 2.96. The classic Two-Stage structure has 14K parameters. The classic Two-Stage structure has 388M MACs. Removing the Large Kernel Extractor decreased PESQ to 2.79. Removing Channel Attention decreased PESQ to 2.86. Removing the Learnable-Sigmoid Gate decreased PESQ to 2.97. Removing the Consistency Loss decreased PESQ to 2.96. Using only Consistency Magnitude Loss resulted in a PESQ of 3.05. Using P=1 resulted in a PESQ of 3.28. Using P=200 resulted in a PESQ of 3.41. Using P=400 resulted in a PESQ of 3.04. Using only complex loss resulted in a PESQ of 2.60.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The Dense-TS framework achieves better performance in later stages due to a smoother loss landscape. Dense connections in narrower models address the early convergence limitations of the baseline model. The MVGB enhances feature extraction by incorporating global, channel, and local perspectives. Relying on Metric Loss to improve objective metrics may negatively impact subjective perception. The Consistency Magnitude Loss is preferred for reconstructing speech signals without introducing distortions. The model is well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained environments due to its compact size.

Contradictions And Limitations
While PESQ scores increase with higher Metric Loss weights, spectral distances also increase. When the Metric Loss weight is too large, training fails. A pseudohallucination distortion is introduced at high Metric Loss weights, affecting perceptual quality. The model does not use complex spectra or phase spectra due to parameter limitations. The source codes will be released after paper acceptance.

Claims
Dense-TSNet is the first speech enhancement model to achieve competitive performance with approximately 10k parameters. The model has a size of only 14K parameters. It is the first to achieve a speech enhancement model with approximately 10k parameters. Other lightweight models like CCFNet(Lite) have 160K parameters. This makes the model suitable for edge devices like smartphones.
The Dense-TS architecture improves upon the classic Two-Stage architecture by providing a smoother loss landscape. The Dense-TS framework can achieve a better performance in the later stages. This is attributed to the smoother loss landscape provided by dense connections. The classic Two-Stage structure converges faster in the early stages. This addresses the early convergence limitations of narrow lightweight models.

Data And Code Availability
Source codes will be released after paper acceptance. Audio samples can be found at the provided GitHub link.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Ablation studies were conducted on the MVGB module design. Removing the Large Kernel Extractor decreased PESQ from 3.05 to 2.79. Removing Channel Attention decreased PESQ from 3.05 to 2.86. Removing the Learnable-Sigmoid Gate decreased PESQ from 3.05 to 2.97. Removing the Consistency Loss decreased PESQ from 3.05 to 2.96. The study validated the impact of using Metric Loss on objective evaluation metrics.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 illustrates the overall architecture of Classic Two-Stage and Dense-TS. Figure 2 shows the internal details of the LKE, LSG, and CA. Figure 3 shows the training criteria of the proposed Dense-TSNet. Figure 4 shows the training curves for Dense-TS and Classic-TS. Table I compares the performance with other methods on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset. Table II presents the ablation study results. Table III studies the effect of the loss function. Figure 5 shows training curves for different Metric Loss weights.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network with 14K parameters. 2. The strongest evidence is the PESQ score of 3.05, outperforming the classic Two-Stage structure. 3. The future path involves exploring methods for further compressing model size.
